page: UpCloud STARTER-1xCPU-2GB is an entry-level virtual server built on the KVM hypervisor. It features a single shared vCPU mapped to one physical core and one thread, utilizing the x86_64 AMD EPYC 9575F processor clocked at 2.0 GHz. The hardware configuration includes 2.0 GB of RAM, 20 GB of local SSD storage, and one complimentary public IPv4 address. The CPU architecture supports advanced instruction sets such as AVX-512 (including AVX512F, AVX512_VNNI, and AVX512_BF16) and cryptographic acceleration via AES, VAES, and SHA_NI.

Benchmark data reveals highly polarized performance characteristics. Due to its single-core shared allocation, the server excels in single-threaded operations, achieving top-tier (top 10%) results in stress-ng single-core CPU performance, single-threaded gzip compression (39.04 GB/sec), and single-threaded bzip3 decompression (17.41 GB/sec). Conversely, multi-core and memory-bound benchmarks are weak. The server registers bottom 25% performance in multi-core stress-ng, Passmark CPU tests, Redis SET operations (3.49 million operations/sec), and static web serving throughput (5.44 GB/sec). Memory performance is particularly constrained, with the Passmark memory score falling into the bottom 10% and read-only memory bandwidth categorized as weak.

From a cost-efficiency perspective, this server represents a low-cost entry point suitable for workloads that do not require sustained multi-core processing or high memory throughput. The resource profile is highly optimized for single-threaded utility scripts, lightweight background workers, basic development or testing environments, and low-traffic static web serving. It is not suitable for database hosting, large language model inference, or memory-intensive applications due to the severe performance trade-offs in memory bandwidth and multi-core execution.
